licence.plates: The facsimile plates are copyrighted pages of the Norton/Liber Novus facsimile (W. W. Norton, 2009). The site’s Commons-only provenance law applies to anything shipped or committed: the plates therefore never enter git and never enter dist. They are referenced as LOCAL-ONLY runtime assets, read at runtime from the owner’s own vault copy over a dev-server-only route; any served build degrades gracefully to a cited note.
licence.text: The mode’s translated text comes from the vault’s Red Book harvest (Reader-edition English, folio/ms/pdf-cited) and follows the vault’s quotation law; translation quotes are cited to the Reader pagination as the vault cites them.
licence.vaultPathNote: The plate directory lives inside the Jung archetypal-field vault, which this repo never writes to.

plates.license: © Foundation of the Works of C. G. Jung
plates.note: Plate files are named for the facsimile’s own pdf pages, p0014–p0223; the vault’s plate mapping (plate pNNNN = ms page NNNN − 31, once the manuscript numbering begins) is the vault’s, not ours.

mode.title: The Red Book
mode.subtitle: Liber Novus, 1913–1930 · Jung’s own record of the descent
mode.subject: jung
mode.oneLine: The folio walk through Liber Novus — Jung’s own hand throughout.

sections.name: The flood and the refound soul
sections.oneLine: October–December 1913: the visions break in, and Jung answers the summons.

sections.name: Siegfried
sections.oneLine: The hero shot dead at the foot of a mountain — the first killing.

sections.name: Elijah and Salome
sections.oneLine: The prophet and the blind pleasure: Logos and Eros as living figures.

sections.name: The Red One
sections.oneLine: The joy of the serious person: the devil met on the road.

sections.name: The desert
sections.oneLine: The desert of the self, the four horses of the sun, the greening remains.

sections.name: Izdubar
sections.oneLine: The bull-man lamed by science, carried westward like an egg.

sections.name: The egg
sections.oneLine: The god incubated in the egg, and reborn as the sun.

sections.name: Philemon and the second layer
sections.oneLine: The magician with four keys, the mandalas, the lapis — the years of images.

sections.name: The Sermones
sections.oneLine: Philemon preaches to the dead: Septem Sermones ad Mortuos, 1916.

stops.plateCaption: fol. i(v): "Der Weg des Kommenden" — the great D holds a flooded lowland under a starred night sky.

/ii(r) spread): illuminated initial D of "Die Wiederfindung der Seele Cap I" — a white bird (the soul) on a dark blue ground — heading the chapter; lower right the S initial of "Seele und Gott Cap II."

/iv(r)): two paintings — above, a small dark panel with a glowing red sun-disc in a cavernous field; below, a larger blue-gray cave scene with a white-robed figure bending toward a red radiant form. The chapter initial "Höllenfahrt in die Zukunft Cap V" shows a horned red goggle-face (lion-serpent countenance).
ms p. 124: "Die drei Prophezeyungen. Cap. XVIII", the D initial on a blue-green ground.

/iv(v)): top left, framed illumination of a radiant golden sun-star flanked by two robed figures (the white-silk garden); mid-page the heading "Heldenmord. Cap VII"; lower left, a framed mountain landscape at dawn with a tiny chariot-figure on the pass (the murder scene); below, "Des Gottes Empfängnis Cap VIII" with flowering border panel.

/v(r)): a full illuminated page — the proclamation set in white script on a deep red-blue diagonally striped frame, a compass/wind-rose star at the head, a chalice at the foot; opposite, a painted border of red flowers on orange ground.

/vi(r)): the famous painting atop the chapter — night-blue mountains, a white-domed columned house at right, Elijah in white-blue robe leading red-robed Salome toward the door, a white bird on the ground before them, and red serpents writhing around all four sides of the frame; above, "MYSTERIUM" in gold Gothic on a red-gold chevron band over the great B initial "Begegnung. Cap. IX."
): tiny figures in white and red within the Auflösung initial; the full scene is text-borne — the only surviving image evidence of the mystery in this range.
/v(v)): "Die Belehrung Cap X" — great blue B initial hung with red flame-spikes (the Buddha in the circle of fire) in a dense text spread.

/vi(v)): "Die Auflösung Cap XI" — illuminated initial inset with a miniature painting of white- and red-robed figures (the serpents' meeting), red marginalia; the book's own "finis partis primi" follows at fol. vii(r) (plate p0029).
illuminated D of "Das Schloß im Walde. Cap. II" — a night-blue castle with lit windows and moon above dark water, painted inside the initial.

— the Liber Secundus title "DIE BILDER DES IRRENDEN" beneath a great D containing a single red EYE on mosaic-tile ground, a red-blue serpent zigzagging down its edge; p0033.jpg (LS p.2) — "Der Rote Cap I" initial painting: tiny green-clad Jung on a red tower, a huge red wing-like shape sweeping the blue sky over water.
text pages in Jung's brown-black hand with red rubrics for the tramp's speeches — the Kiniematograph dialogue; no painting in this chapter.
text page with small red-and-green initial at "Ich schreite um..." — the sea-of-blood passage and the note "es war die zweite Nacht des Jahres 1914" are text-borne here.
/iii(r)): illuminated D of "Die Wüste Cap. IV" — a small human figure standing within the initial on deep color grounds.

the great Gothic display page of Dies II — "Wenn du schläfst, so ruhst du, wie all das was je war..." in large black and red textura — the sleep through the millennia and the temple chants; no figurative painting.
display page of ch. vii — "Nach Flucht kommt das Licht, damit die Ferne errettet werde von dem Tod" in large textura with A initials; the greening is text-borne in this range.

a frontal standing giant filling the page — black-bearded, crowned with bull horns, eyes wide, wearing a blue-black scale corselet and a red kilt patterned with cuneiform-like ornament; his right hand plants a double-axe (the bull-slaying labrys) point-down. The entire ground is a tiled textile of pale-blue serpents interlaced with brown winged dragons on blue; stepped ziggurat-like brick flanks descend at both sides, rows of dark serpents crawling on them; at the bottom, behind a fence, a tiny white-robed human figure with raised arms faces the colossus. Jung's margin inscription records that the image was painted around Christmas 1913 — i.e. BEFORE the Jan 8, 1914 fantasy it "illustrates": the painting led the text.

"Erster Tag. Cap. VIII." — the great E initial on deep-blue starfield with a golden rayed sun-disc at its center and a red-orange serpent coiling down the panel's right edge; the meeting scene itself is text-borne.

— "Der mächtige fiel, er liegt am Boden" set in a Ravenna-style red mosaic border of tiny blue figure-tiles, beneath the great apostrophe "Ach, herrlich äußerlich schöner Freund... wie ganz eins sind Schlange und Gott"; p0075.jpg (LS p.44) — the wide night painting: star-filled sky between two dark brick pillars over blue mountains, a band of glowing fire-colored light at the horizon, a tiny dark figure with raised arms before it (Images 44/45; Atharva-veda 4,1,4 virility charm cited in legend — the healing of the wounded bull-god).

Full-page illumination on a dense red ground: bold blue, white and ochre totemic meander-ornament frames a central blackletter text column opening "Weihnacht ist gekommen: der Gott ist im Ei..." — under a blue cloud-arc holding a many-domed temple and a lotus; at the base, a golden egg rests in a dark vessel-niche. Corner-marked "50".

Rubricated title "die eröffnung des eies · Cap. XI"; a square gold block holding a red-and-black interlaced fantastic animal initial A opens the blackletter text: "Am Abend des dritten tages kniete ich auf dem Teppich nieder u öffnete behutsam das Ei. Wie ein Rauch stieg es daraus empor u plötzlich steht Izdubar vor mir / riesengroß u verwandelt u vollkommen..." — followed by the sun-monologue in verse lines.

"Der Anachoret. Cap. IV. Dies. I." — the great illuminated D set inside a square panel of Ravenna-like mosaic: interlaced red-orange-purple maze bands around a blue field; the eye-opening page of the desert cycle.

A four-lobed black-outlined mandala: at center a blue eight-pointed star on a brown-black ring segmented like a zodiac with red/white counter-chips; around it eight scroll-filled lobes in blue, yellow and white beneath red bands; at the cardinal points four small roundels — top: white-robed old man seated in contemplation; left: woman in red robe; right: woman in blue robe; bottom: dark chthonic figure against purple. Corner-marked "105".

Full-page painting: a black serpent patterned with white eye-spots winds up from lower left, head at upper right above a cluster of red cloud-blossoms ringed in red, over a swirling purple-red-and-olive vegetal ground. Blackletter legend above; corner-marked "111".

Left half: a tall vertical serpent-dragon in scaled greens, small human arms sprouting in tiers along its body, a black eye and red fanged open mouth at the top, labelled "ATMAVICTV"; a pale sun disc floats above. Right half: a dense blackletter text block; beneath it the three small figures with Latin labels; the blackletter legend runs across the foot. Corner-marked "117".

Gold ground. Upper left: a white domed temple on a small cloud. Upper right: a dark-haired man in a green-and-white striped robe stands on a wide blue-and-white disc beneath a red sun disc, pouring a zigzag stream of holy water from a vessel. Below, dark red-tipped flowers rise from a black earthen band in which the prone dragon's body lies traced with lightning squiggles; water drips onto the blossoms. Corner-marked "123".
ms p. 139: "Der Zauberer. Cap. XXI", the D set in a violet lattice.

A monumental horned mask-face fills the sheet: orange-red speckled skin, large eyes with blue lids and rayed irises, shaggy black mane and long pointed beard, small dark horns. The ground is cracked cream-and-rose stone strewn with dark fossils — an ammonite, a crinoid frond, bone fragments, a trilobite-like shell, a horn. Inscription "a der MCMXIX" at lower left; legend in blackletter across the foot.

Square black frame enclosing an orange-red lattice of interlocking triangles; white star-points glint at the lattice crossings. At the center a dark-green eight-pointed star/rose-window holds a white-and-rose layered rosette "like ruby-colored glass." Blackletter dedication beneath. Corner-marked "159".

Full page of blackletter dialogue in red ("I:") and green (the devil's initial) alternating — the page ends "ich glaube / du wirst bald am aussterben" ("I believe [the dead] will soon become extinct," pdf p353). Corner-marked "162".
ms p. 154: Philemon, winged, haloed, in a blue and red robe above the garden.
Plain cream page, dense blue ink in Jung's everyday script within a ruled margin, "1959" at top left. The final plate of the facsimile (p0223) is a blank endpaper.

genesis.name: Philemon
genesis.words: It was he who taught me psychic objectivity, the reality of the psyche
genesis.doctrine: The wise old man named (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious ¶79); the meaning-regulator (Mysterium Coniunctionis ¶313); Mercurius-senex (Alchemical Studies ¶218); the murdered senex via Goethe (Psychology and Alchemy ¶561).

genesis.name: The anima
genesis.doctrine: Salome → Kali → “case Z” in the Kore essay (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious ¶361, ¶371); the ladder (The Practice of Psychotherapy ¶361).

genesis.name: The wise old man / mana-personality
genesis.words: An old man stood before me. He looked like one of the old prophets
genesis.doctrine: The naming (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious ¶79); the mana-personality chapter (Two Essays on Analytical Psychology ¶377–80); 1925: “the wise man, the medicine man, the mana man” (Analytical Psychology: Notes of the 1925 Seminar pdf p113).

genesis.name: The serpent
genesis.words: If one waits long enough, one sees how the Gods all change into serpents and underworld dragons in the end.
genesis.doctrine: The whole serpent-row chain: lowest-and-highest (Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self ¶293); serpent-Christ (Psychology and Alchemy ¶184); serpens mercurialis (Alchemical Studies ¶448–49).

genesis.name: Anthropos / Izdubar
genesis.words: this is Izdubar, the mighty, the bull-man
genesis.doctrine: The renewed God = renewed attitude (Psychological Types ¶301, editor n.137); Anthropos = self (Alchemical Studies ¶269); Aion’s Anthropos chapters.

genesis.name: The mandala and the self
genesis.words: And that is the self, the wholeness of the personality
genesis.doctrine: Mandala doctrine (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious, “Mandala Symbolism” — the ms 105 mandala published as “a male patient’s”); the self-symbol (Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self ¶426).

genesis.name: The aeon doctrine
genesis.words: the month of the fish will soon be over
genesis.doctrine: Aion 1951: the Platonic month (Aion ¶135–49) and the aeon thesis of the foreword — the Red Book is the doctrine’s earliest witness.

genesis.name: The pleroma
genesis.words: Now hear: I begin with nothingness. Nothingness is the same as the fullness
genesis.doctrine: Tao (Psychological Types ¶363); Bardo-pleroma (Psychology and Religion: West and East ¶629); unus mundus (Mysterium Coniunctionis ¶660).

genesis.name: The transcendent function
genesis.words: we are real and not symbols
genesis.doctrine: The 1916 essay (The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche pdf p79) and the 1921 definition (Psychological Types ¶184).

genesis.name: The war prophecies → the Turn
genesis.words: it is completely real, and it will come to pass
genesis.doctrine: The 1918 forecast (Civilization in Transition ¶17); the possession doctrine (Civilization in Transition ¶437).

genesis.name: The new God in the relative / Abraxas
genesis.words: Effectiveness... is a God above God... We call him by his name ABRAXAS
genesis.doctrine: The Christ↔Antichrist doctrine (Aion ch. III, Aion ¶76); the anti-privatio-boni argument of Aion and Answer to Job.

genesis.name: The divine child
genesis.words: I have received your sprout, you who are to come!
genesis.doctrine: The child-archetype essay (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious, 1940); individuation’s beginning (editor n.123).

genesis.name: The shadow
genesis.words: he was my joy, the joy of the serious person
genesis.doctrine: The shadow essays (The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious / Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self ¶13–19); the flaying before one’s own I, later read as shadow-confrontation (editor n.8, citing The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious).

genesis.name: Christ ↔ Antichrist
genesis.words: The image of the Antichrist, which has come down to us from the ancients, announces the new God
genesis.doctrine: Aion ch. III: “an imitating spirit of evil who follows in Christ’s footsteps like a shadow” (Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self ¶76); “an inexorable psychological law” (¶77).
